messages:
sara-support: FYI customer reported sudden 429s from their Dedicated pool after a billing plan update. Happening across all endpoints, spikes at ~2 req/s per tenant. Can someone take a look?

ops-bot: Alert: dedicated-pool:tenant-429-rate detected for tenant=acme-corp, pool=eu-west-dedicated, 2023-11-15T14:02:01Z :warning:

mike-dedicated: on it. tenant id and last plan id? any repro steps?

sara-support: tenant=acme-corp, plan_tag changed from "starter-hourly" -> "startup-monthly" during migration. customer says it went through our billing API at 13:58 UTC. Quick repro: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rwd-2-small","input":"hello"}' and we see 429 body: `\{"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"code\":429\}`. Attached logs: ```2023-11-15T14:01:59Z request_id=abcd123 tenant=acme-corp route=/v1/generate pool=eu-west-dedicated status=429 throttled_by=per-tenant-rate-limit rate_key=plan:startup-monthly:token-per-hour```

nina-eng: the rate_key shows `token-per-hour` denom — note the plan tag used to be `minute` denom on starter. If the plan conversion pipeline mis-tagged denom when migrating to monthly, we might be treating their quota as much lower (hour vs minute) -> effectively 60x tighter. Could explain sudden 429s.

ian-platform: also saw autoscaler logs: `quietpool warmup disabled for pool eu-west-dedicated` immediately after the plan change; autoscale didn't spin new capacity because routing layer thinks tenant is rate-limited, not queued. Might be two issues: quota conversion + autoscale suppression.

mike-dedicated: good catch. @nina-eng can you confirm mapping in the plan-conversion job? Which service owns that mapping? I can patch throttle keys to temporarily lift limits for this tenant if needed.

nina-eng: plan-conversion job is convsvc v2.0.1 (team: billing). Quick grep: `convsvc --dump-tag-mapping --tag startup-monthly` returns `denom:hour tokens_per_unit:1000` but expected `denom:minute tokens_per_unit:60`. Looks like a migration script used legacy defaults.

mike-dedicated: okay immediate mitigation: run: ```./admin-tools adjust-tenant-quota --tenant acme-corp --rate-key plan:startup-monthly:token-per-hour --multiplier 60 --reason "emergency quota lift while billing migration rollback"``` that will scale their effective units up until billing fixes mapping. I'll also add a temporary override for the dedicated pool routing so we don't prematurely evict.

sara-support: customer approved. Running step now. I'll post before/after. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Job started: adjust-tenant-quota id=job-8422 user=mike-dedicated

sara-support: After command: requests now succeed, latency normal. Example response: `200 OK` and generation token usage increments. No more 429s for last 10m.

ian-platform: Follow-up: we should add a guard in autoscaler so plan changes don't auto-suppress warmup for dedicated pools. Filing an infra ticket.

nina-eng: I'll open a billing migration PR to fix denom mapping and add unit tests. Also adding a migration audit that emits a high-severity alert if denom flips between minute/hour/day.

mike-dedicated: Recording postmortem: root cause = plan-tag translation bug in convsvc during monthly migration -> denom changed from minute -> hour. Secondary impact = autoscaler suppression logic treated the tenant as rate-limited and prevented warmup. Mitigation = emergency quota multiplier + routing override + rollback of bad tag mapping.

sara-support: Customer notified and thanked for quick fix. Marking as resolved on our side but leaving infra/billing tickets open.

mike-dedicated: TL;DR repro steps for ops: 1) reproduce 429 with curl after plan swap 2) check logs for `throttled_by=per-tenant-rate-limit` and rate_key denom 3) run adjust-tenant-quota multiplier 60 4) rollback plan tag in convsvc and deploy hotfix 5) verify autoscaler warmup behavior

ops-bot: Incident resolved: dedicated-throttle-acme-6072468000 status=resolved by mike-dedicated at 2023-11-15T14:17:05Z :white_check_mark:
